  • In the end it also points to another thing.
  • Industry observers note that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

Industry observers note that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

Sources indicate that “It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

It has been revealed that was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

According to recent reports, that is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

Sources indicate that the hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Industry observers note that ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Recent findings suggest that can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick mentioned this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

It has been revealed that having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Industry observers note that bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1.

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area revealed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

In a recent development, but after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm.

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick indicates he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

Recent findings suggest that “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Recent findings suggest that carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick mentioned. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

In a recent development, the Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

It has been revealed that “It notes a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

In a recent development, “It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports, he noted: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

Sources indicate that “They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

According to recent reports, “It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and stated he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

Cardiff City square off against Preston North End on Tuesday evening looking for the win that will create further distance between themselves and the relegation zone.

At a time when the Bluebirds sit in 15th position in the Championship table, Preston remain bottom despite a two-match unbeaten run.

After 15 goals featured in Cardiff's two matches before the international break, it was anyone's guess how they would perform against in-form Norwich City on Saturday.

Taking the lead at Carrow Road put the Bluebirds on the way to a statement victory, but Norwich battled back to earn a 2-1 win.

Nevertheless, Brian Barry-Murphy will continue to take the positives from having 18 points from their first 16 games since finishing second in last season's League One.

Although they remain with just two points from eight away contests, they remain unbeaten across the same amount of fixtures at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Twenty-one goals - the second-best return in home Championship games in 2026-27 - have been scored, with Cardiff posting four wins and four draws in South Wales.

Many felt that Preston could have been cut adrift at the bottom of the Championship table ahead of their game with Southampton on November 7.

Instead, Graham Alexander's side have impressively accumulated four points from a double-header of the Saints and West Ham United.

Not only did Preston record a 1-0 win over Southampton, they held West Ham to a 1-1 draw at the London Stadium on Saturday.

That result meant that Preston put together a two-match unbeaten streak in the Championship for the first time since April 11.

Despite the growing optimism at Deepdale, Preston are still six points behind 21st position.

Perry Ng and Gabriel Osho are expected to remain sidelined through injury, along with Dylan Lawlor and Calum Chambers.

With Andrija Vukcevic suffering an injury against West Ham, Brad Potts is expected to deputise at left wing-back.

Stanley Mills and Andrew Moran also sustained complications at the London Stadium, with Ed Nolan and Greg Docherty in line to feature in a much-changed lineup.

Roy Keane has predicted the biggest threat to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining the Premier League title is unlikely to come from any of their traditional rivals.

The Gunners displayed unfamiliar signs of vulnerability at St James’ Park on Saturday evening where they let a half-time lead slip, before eventually battling back to earn a 2-2 draw.

The loss of two points was compounded by an injury to goalkeeper David Raya who is now nervously anticipating the results of a forthcoming MRI scan on his damaged arm.

Manchester City’s failure to win at home against Fulham meant the failure to cling onto the lead Arsenal gained through Eberechi Eze’s first-half opener represented a missed opportunity.

With Enzo Maresca’s side in the midst of a disappointing run and the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool struggling to come to terms with the demands of their new managers, Arsenal are widely expected to defend the title they won back in May.

Indeed, their nearest challengers at present are Brighton, who are thriving under the management of Fabian Hurzeler, and Keane sees no reason why the Seagulls can’t continue to mount a challenge.

‘At this moment, yes,’ Keane told Sky Sports when asked if Brighton could emerge as the only team capable of preventing Arsenal from claiming back-to-back titles.

‘That’s because of the form they’re in, they’re goal threat and defensively they’re very, very good.

‘They’ve got a top quality manager but obviously over the next couple of months the pressure and injuries and whatever (will come).

‘They’ve got a young team and have a lack of experience. But at this moment in time they’ve got to enjoy it and keep that pressure on Arsenal.’.

Hurzeler, who masterminded a 3-0 win over the Gunners back in September, has plenty of admirers and was recently linked with the Manchester United job.

‘His time will come,’ Keane remarked when it was put to him that the German would’ve represented a better appointment than Mauricio Pochettino.

‘We talk about Poch getting close a few times and sliding doors moments. He’s done a great job and Brighton and if he left now you’d be looking at him and thinking he should’ve stuck at it a bit more.

Industry observers note that ‘We talk about loyalty in football and it’s got to work both ways. So I’m glad he continuing at Brighton and hopefully they can continue having a good season.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare debut as Manchester United manager as he watched his newly introduced side fall to a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

The Red Devils endured a horrendous start to the match, with Leny Yoro sent off inside eight minutes and the hosts two goals up inside the opening quarter of an hour on Merseyside.

Dominik Szoboszlai slammed home the resulting free kick after Yoro had denied Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity, who latched onto a mistake from Matthijs de Ligt, who misjudged a ball clipped over the top.

It was two not long after as Florian Wirtz hooked home with an improvised left-footed volley after Rio Ngumoha had darted beyond Diogo Dalot as if he weren’t there down the left, dinking it into the middle for the German to slot in via the crossbar.

Isak produced a superb centre-forward’s performance but was wasteful with his finishing, and he sliced wide after another De Ligt error in the second half, and he was denied by Senne Lammens, who parried well after a brilliant break through the middle from Barcola.

It was three after the hour, as Ngumoha slotted home a deserved third after Barcola had left Lisandro Martinez for dead, burning away from the recovering Bruno Fernandes before squaring for his opposite winger to slide in the killer.

Substitute Victor Munoz emphatically slammed in the fourth after more superb work from Wirtz, who found the Spaniard having won the ball deep in United territory.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino could only watch on in horror as the enormity of the task he has undertaken became crystal clear to him. For now, his men sit 19th in the Premier League table, firmly mired in the relegation zone.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leny Yoro was sent off to mark a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United manager at Liverpool.
  • The Argentine head coach could only watch on in horror as his fresh side were thumped 4-0 at Anfield, thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.
  • The Reds took full advantage of their visitors’ red card on eight minutes, when Yoro was penalised for hauling down Alexander Isak as the Swede sped through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leny Yoro was sent off to mark a nightmare start for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United manager at Liverpool.

The Argentine head coach could only watch on in horror as his fresh side were thumped 4-0 at Anfield, thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

The Reds took full advantage of their visitors’ red card on eight minutes, when Yoro was penalised for hauling down Alexander Isak as the Swede sped through on goal.

It stemmed from a Matthijs de Ligt mistake, after the Dutchman, making his first Premier League appearance in over a year after a persistent back injury, misjudged the flight of a clipped ball over the top from Jeremy Jacquet.

Isak seized upon the error, Yoro failed to cover his central defensive partner in time, and the 20-year-old was forced to fell the advancing striker before he could get a shot away at Senne Lammens’ goal.

The Premier League Match Centre explained the decision to send the young French defender for an early bath with a post on its social media channels.

“The referee’s call of red card to Yoro for denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO) was checked and confirmed by VAR,” the statement read.

According to recent reports, referee Sam Barratt explained to his video assistant referee: “It's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside [the box], red card, DOGSO.”.

The VAR replied: “Defender bundles into him into the back, gets too tight, I think it's a foul.”.

Yoro’s last-ditch challenge ultimately went punished regardless, as Szoboszlai stepped up to slam home the resulting free kick, arrowing into Lammens’ far corner to open the scoring.

The result leaves United mired in the Premier League relegation zone, in 19th place, after just one win in 12 games in all competitions.

"Very painful, it hurts a lot," he said. "Coming to our rivals and losing is always bad. It's a difficult moment for us, but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation.

According to recent reports, "We still created a lot of chances to try and do something in the game, even with one player less. Unfortunately, we were not able to avoid two more goals in the second half.

According to recent reports, "We were very brave. In some moments, we lost the ball, but we were trying to play, we were trying to do something in the game, we were not afraid.

In a recent development, "You want to get results, but today, it was not possible for us. There were a lot of things we can look at, and I saw a lot of character from the team. The result won't show that, but I am very proud of everyone in the dressing room.".

Yoro's red card was the earliest shown to a United player in a Premier League match, with the defender penalised for a professional foul on Alexander Isak.

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

‘When I saw Matthijs de Ligt’s name on the teamsheet, I have to be honest with you, I was absolutely stunned,’ Neville mentioned on Sky Sports’ commentary of the match.

‘The reason I was stunned was because of this: if you watched him against Como four weeks ago, he was very much well of it.

‘That is just a basic ball over the top of him. It’s his problem to start with.’.

Though De Ligt was the main focus of Neville’s criticism, Yoro did not escape without receiving some barbs of his own.

‘Leny Yoro can be further across but if you look at De Ligt in this channel, he’s miles away from him,’ Neville added.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Yoro should be across, yes, he can get further around. He has to cover and he doesn’t. He reacts late, his anticipation is really poor.

‘And because he doesn’t play the ball, Yoro, it could be outside the box but it is a red card.

‘It’s so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these kinds of mistakes.’.

According to Neville, Yoro had displayed great ‘naivety’ in getting himself sent off so early in the Premier League contest.

‘He’s not happy with it, Mauricio Pochettino,’ the ex-England international continued.

‘You could argue with it, Isak just delays slightly to make sure that Yoro runs into the back of him.

‘But unfortunately, when you’re a young defender, you’re going to get caught like that and it’s naivety.’.

Switching his focus back to De Ligt, Neville said the Netherlands international had likely been ‘exposed’ as a result of playing so little football over the last 12 months.

Sources indicate that ‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough,’ he went on.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.

It has been revealed that ‘I have to say, Yoro’s positioning covering is really poor. It’s poor.

It has been revealed that ‘Yoro has got to be across and around the other centre-back. You’ve got to cover your mate and he doesn’t. It’s really just bad all round from Manchester United.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’.

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘It’s as bad as it gets from two centre-backs,’ the former Liverpool and England defender stated.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino made unwanted history on his debut as Manchester United manager on Sunday.

The Argentine watched on in anguish as his fresh side were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield, thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

It started horrendously for the 54-year-old as Leny Yoro was sent off just eight minutes in for denying Alexander Isak a clear goal-scoring opportunity, and that was verified by the Premier League Match Centre on social media.

Pochettino, the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach, has become the first manager in Premier League history whose team has conceded twice and had a man sent off in the first half of their first match in charge.

There was more positive history for the victors, with Ngumoha breaking the fixture’s record for youngest goalscorer as he slid in the third from Bradley Barcola’s breath-taking break, as the Frenchman squared for his opposite winger to slot home beyond Senne Lammens.

He overtook Michael Owen, who was spotted pitchside on TV punditry duty, at just 18 years and 85 days.

The young England star also became the youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a Premier League game since Owen on Boxing Day back in 1997, when the striker did the same against Leeds United.

The result leaves Liverpool fourth in the Premier League table, seven points off league leaders Arsenal, while Pochettino’s United are mired in the relegation zone, having won just once in 12 matches in all competitions.

Separated by just one point but nine places in the Champions League rankings, Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund cross paths in Tuesday's league-phase encounter at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners boast a marginal advantage over their German counterparts, having taken 10 points from their opening four fixtures against Napoli, Bayern Munich, Lille and Slavia Prague.

Meanwhile, Niko Kovac has guided Dortmund to victories over Real Betis, Sabah FK and Villarreal, albeit while also overseeing a dampening 1-0 defeat away to Bodo/Glimt on matchday two.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

From eight previous Champions League meetings between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund, the North London giants hold the bragging rights, but only just.

Indeed, the Gunners have won four of their eight head-to-heads compared to three for BVB, while only one previous encounter has ended all square.

The 2002-03 season marked the inaugural competitive meetings between Arsenal and Dortmund, who each got one over the other in the group stage; the Gunners triumphed 2-0 at Highbury as Dennis Bergkamp and Freddie Ljungberg netted in the second half, before Dortmund prevailed 2-1 at home, courtesy of a winner from future Arsenal fan favourite Tomas Rosicky.

Not until the 2011-12 season would the two teams butt heads again, but they were subsequently drawn to face each other in three of the next four Champions League group-stage campaigns.

Dortmund and Arsenal drew 1-1 at Signal Iduna Park in September 2011, but Arsene Wenger's men prevailed 2-1 at the Emirates two months later thanks to a Robin van Persie brace.

Both sides then beat each other away from home for the first time in the 2013-14 campaign, Dortmund earning a 2-1 Emirates triumph before Arsenal won 1-0 in Germany, Aaron Ramsey nodding home the only goal.

The 2014-15 campaign also saw Arsenal and Dortmund trade blows and victories, as Jurgen Klopp inspired BVB to a 2-0 success at the Westfalenstadion, before Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez sealed an identical Gunners win in North London.

Arteta captained Arsenal to victory in their November 2014 Emirates showdown, but that would prove to be the Spaniard's final senior appearance of that season, as he picked up a serious calf injury in the second half before also undergoing ankle surgery.

Nov 26, 2014: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League).

Aberdeen's new manager is a proven overachiever with a big personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1343 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.

Stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event. While unquestionably a successful manager with Motherwell and St Mirren, there was always a lingering doubt about whether his skill set would work at a bigger club with different expectations in terms of style of play. And so it proved.

What didn’t help the Northern Irishman was the perception that those who employed him weren’t exactly bowled over by him in the first place, either.

Robinson would have been a hard enough sell to the Dons support had he been unveiled a few days after Jimmy Thelin departed the scene in January.

That it took them 67 days to deliver confirmation of the appointment – after the club had dalliances with Eirik Horneland and Sandro Schwarz – was hardly a ringing endorsement of their faith in him.

Recent findings suggest that the contrast with the process to appoint Mario Frick is striking. Robinson was sacked two days after a four-goal home thrashing by Hibernian. Five days later, the former Liechtenstein international was named by the Pittodrie club as the fresh head coach.

Sources indicate that after the saga at the start of the year which reflected well on no one, Aberdeen, to give them their dues, knew what they wanted and saw Frick as a hand-in-glove fit. So, what led them so swiftly to his door?

Mario Frick is unveiled at Pittodrie and immediately vowed to transform the club's fortunes.

The 52-year-old, essentially, is a head coach who fits in with the overarching strategy Aberdeen identified several years ago.

This has been lost along the way as poor results have seen a churn of individuals occupy the dug-out, many of whom were square pegs in round holes. This, the club believe, has been why the recruitment has been so random and ineffective.

There’s been little joined-up thinking, as evidenced by the summer window which saw 15 players arrive, many of whom were sub-standard or clearly not part of Robinson’s plan.

The intention always was for the head coach to work in tandem with the sporting director and chief executive rather than independently of them.

While Frick will have a say on what players arrive and depart this January, the conversations around the identity of the team and what’s required to improve it will be three-way.

At Luzern, Frick was happy to trust the judgment of director of football Remo Meyer on such matters.

His willingness to forge the same relationship with Aberdeen’s sporting director, Lutz Pfannenstiel, was the light bulb moment for chief executive Adrian Bevington and chairman Dave Cormack.

Frick earned 125 caps for Liechtenstein and scored 16 goals for the European minnows.

In keeping with the much-vaunted ‘continental’ model, Pfannenstiel and head of recruitment Darren Mowbray will largely identify players to fit the system. Frick will then be tasked with making it all work.

The proposal is for the squad to be closely aligned with the head coach’s needs rather than assembling the rag bag of players who’ve come in the three windows since Thelin won the Scottish Cup.

There’s much beyond Frick’s willingness to defer matters of player identification to others which caught the eye of the board, however.

Although very much a modern and forward-thinking coach, he’s vastly experienced in the game.

As a player, he turned out for Swiss clubs including St Gallen, Basel, Zurich and Grasshopper.

He became the first Liechtensteiner to play professionally in Italy with AC Arezzo before signing for Verona, Ternana and Siena.

Across 125 internationals, he became Liechtenstein’s all-time top scorer with 16 goals, including one against Scotland at Hampden in 2010, the infamous game which saw Stephen McManus ride to the rescue with a 90th-minute winner.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington welcomes new manager Frick to Pittodrie.

According to recent reports, being the star man for an underdog may have had something to do with his upbringing. Frick’s father didn’t exactly encourage him to make it as he started out in the game.

According to recent reports, he once revealed in an interview: ‘He told me: ‘There are thousands of talents like you. You won’t make it.’.

His coaching journey began eight years ago with Vaduz, who he succeeded in getting promoted to the Swiss Super League via a play-off.

Appointed head coach of Luzern almost five years ago, he turned the side from relegation candidates into one capable of finishing fourth inside 18 months. There followed finishes of seventh, sixth and seventh place prior to an amicable parting of the ways when his contract expired in May.

Although Frick didn’t win anything, Luzern is not a club which is accustomed to doing so, with their last league title arriving in 1989.

Its supporters still strongly identified with him, though, and recognised that he often got more out of modest resources than he was entitled to.

They enjoyed his significant personality – not scared to wind up opponents in the media and not shy at publicly calling out his own players when they didn’t live up to the standards he’d set.

Frick famously scored for Liechtenstein against Scotland in a 2-1 at Hampden in 2010.

When he left there at the end of last season, the supporters felt the loss of a passionate manager who wore his heart on his sleeve, had no time for egos and stopped at nothing to deliver success.

In the Granite City, he will call out anyone not giving their absolute all every moment they are in a red jersey. And unlike the diplomatic Thelin, the fireworks are likely to be seen in public.

It has been revealed that if his time at Luzern proves prescient, those who resist or disrupt the dressing room will soon be moved on. Those who do their best by him will have nothing to fear, however.

As Italian football fan Fabio Baccarini will gladly attest, although tough and demanding, Frick is also renowned as being a loyal man with a huge heart.

Baccarini, from Reggio Emilia, became fascinated by Frick in the early 2000s while collecting Panini stickers due to the fact that he played for Liechtenstein, a tiny nation he struggled to pronounce.

He wrote so many letters to his various clubs, hoping to arrange a meeting, that Frick initially feared he might be a stalker.

When they first met in 2011 after a game between Liechtenstein and San Marino, the forward presented Baccarini with a signed shirt, gave him his email address and invited him to a match in Vaduz.

And so began an extraordinary friendship which saw Baccarini regularly drive 1,000km to support the minnows and become their de facto mascot.

Sources indicate that three years back, when Hibs travelled to Luzern in the Conference League, the Italian super-fan was unable to find a bed for the night. Frick ensured he got one in the team hotel at no cost.

The newly introduced Pittodrie boss is just the latest to follow in the footsteps of the great Sir Alex Ferguson.

As heartwarming as such tales are, it was, of course, the metrics of on-field success which drew Aberdeen to him.

Frick’s willingness to give young players a chance – another criticism made of Robinson – was a tick against his name.

He’s handed top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career. He appointed Ardon Jashari, who played against Scotland on Monday, his Luzern captain at the age of 20.

He does not appear to be wedded to a particular formation. He mostly played a 4-4-2 with a diamond at Luzern, but he’s very much a pragmatist.

When he takes his bow at Rugby Park on Saturday, he’ll select a system to suit the personnel rather than trying to shoehorn the players into a pre-ordained system.

With just two points separating their team from bottom-side Kilmarnock, how the Red Army could do with witnessing a Super Mario bounce.

Arsenal could face a fresh complication in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with Paris Saint-Germain reportedly considering whether to accelerate their interest in the Frenchman following Desire Doue's serious knee injury.

The European champions were already among the clubs monitoring Kroupi ahead of the January transfer window, but their attacking situation has become considerably more difficult after Doue was stretchered off during Saturday's 3-2 Ligue 1 victory over Nice. PSG confirmed on Sunday that the 21-year-old has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will undergo surgery before the end of November.

According to TEAMtalk transfer correspondent Graeme Bailey, PSG hold a strong interest in the Bournemouth attacker, who is also wanted by Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur. The French champions could now consider stepping up their pursuit, although no formal approach or offer has been reported.

Any attempt to secure the youngster's signature would present a substantial financial challenge. Bournemouth are understood to value Kroupi at upwards of £80m and have shown little willingness to entertain a mid-season departure, despite increasing attention from some of Europe's leading clubs.

Doue's confirmed ACL rupture has left Luis Enrique facing a potentially season-ending absence in a forward line already weakened by the loss of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

According to recent reports, the France international had scored PSG's second goal against Nice before suffering the injury late in the first half. He required treatment on the pitch and was eventually carried off on a stretcher, with Ferran Torres replacing him and subsequently scoring the winning goal.

Luis Enrique warned after the match that the injury was serious, although he stressed that further medical examinations were needed to establish its precise nature.

Industry observers note that those concerns were confirmed on Sunday when PSG declared that Doue had suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. The club also confirmed that the forward would undergo surgery before the end of November.

Although PSG have not announced a definitive recovery timetable, the severity of the injury raises serious doubts about whether Doue will play again this season.

The setback follows Kvaratskhelia's ACL injury during PSG's Champions League victory over Barcelona in October, which has already deprived Enrique of another crucial attacking option.

It has been revealed that paris still possess considerable depth, with Ousmane Dembele, Torres, Manuel Akliouche and Mika Godts among the players available to the Spanish coach. Nevertheless, losing two influential attackers in relatively quick succession could alter the club's approach to the January window.

That is where Kroupi's situation becomes particularly interesting.

Bailey reports that PSG are admirers of the Bournemouth forward and that Doue's injury could encourage them to intensify an interest that existed well before Saturday's events.

Industry observers note that kroupi would not necessarily represent a direct replacement for Doue. Although capable of operating across the attacking line, he is primarily a centre-forward, meaning any move would also reflect a broader decision about how Enrique wishes to reshape his available options.

It has been revealed that there is presently no indication that PSG have opened negotiations with Bournemouth or made Kroupi their preferred January target. The possibility of an accelerated approach remains dependent on the club's assessment of its attacking needs.

For Arsenal, the prospect of renewed PSG interest adds another dimension to an already complicated transfer pursuit.

In a recent development, the Gunners have been following Kroupi's development for several months, while Tottenham have also been linked with the attacker. Barcelona and Bayern Munich are among the other European clubs reportedly keeping a close eye on his progress.

Kroupi's emergence has made him one of Bournemouth's most valuable assets. The former Lorient forward scored 13 Premier League goals last season and has since earned international recognition with France, strengthening his reputation as one of the country's most promising young attacking talents.

In a recent development, however, Bournemouth are under little pressure to sanction an immediate sale. Kroupi remains under contract until June 2030, and the Cherries are determined to benefit from his performances during the remainder of the campaign.

According to recent reports, david Ornstein recently indicated in The Athletic that a January transfer was unlikely, with Bournemouth expected to be more receptive to offers next summer. The journalist also suggested that the player could favour a move abroad when the time comes to leave the Vitality Stadium.

That possibility represents a further concern for Arsenal, particularly given PSG's existing interest and Kroupi's connections with French football.

The financial demands are equally significant. Bournemouth have been linked with an asking price of at least £80m, although other reports have suggested that an even larger offer could be required to secure an agreement.

Those figures reflect the club's negotiating position rather than a confirmed bid from any interested party.

Arsenal's previously reported difficulties in securing a January deal therefore remain relevant regardless of whether PSG decide to make their interest more concrete.

A significant offer from Paris could potentially change the competitive landscape, particularly if the French champions decide that their injury problems justify an expensive winter investment.

In a recent development, yet Bournemouth's position is unlikely to soften simply because another club has suffered an attacking setback. Any January approach would have to overcome the same contractual and financial obstacles facing Arsenal and Tottenham.

For now, PSG's growing need for attacking cover provides a newly introduced consideration in Kroupi's future, but the immediate question for all three interested clubs is whether Bournemouth can be persuaded to discuss a transfer before the summer.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

Logic control of NeuroAxis during closed-loop glucose-responsive neuromodulation. The NeuroAxis-mediated VNS is triggered only after the glucose level exceeds a threshold of five consecutive readings. Once the stimulation condition is met, the system delivers biphasic electrical pulses for 3 min.

Mauricio Pochettino slams ‘unfair’ decision after Man Utd’s defeat to Liverpool

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.
  • Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.
  • The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens swiftly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino noted in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

It has been revealed that ‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field. We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’.

According to recent reports, pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

Industry observers note that ‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

In a recent development, ‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

Recent findings suggest that ‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most important. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone prior to the November international break, when Carrick was relieved of his duties.

Results over the weekend leave the Red Devils second from bottom in the Premier League with just eight points from their first 11 games of the campaign.

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Industry observers note that evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'.

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

Recent findings suggest that evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday.

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm.

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

Whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially announced Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

Industry observers note that 'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the new manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'.

According to recent reports, jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

Industry observers note that 'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'.

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'.

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

During a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said his side could “celebrate at half time” during their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

The Reds ran out easy victors against their fierce rivals on Sunday, with United hoping to snap a miserable run of just one win in 12 matches.

They did not get the desired bounce from the arrival of fresh boss Mauricio Pochettino, who watched his side thrashed at Anfield and go down to ten men in eight minutes after Leny Yoro’s red card, which he bemoaned afterwards.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz netted the goals to hand the hosts a straightforward three points that sees them sit fourth, seven points off league leaders Arsenal.

United, meanwhile, are spiralling and remain in the Premier League relegation zone, in 19th place.

Industry observers note that “I think you can enjoy it, you can see it coming. It's difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half time and enjoy it a little bit and have lovely moments.

Lincoln do have the worst home record in the division, having picked up five points from eight games and shipped more goals than any other side, but they have fared better away from home.

  • Some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s tenth-minute breakthrough and saw the latter shown a straight red card by referee Samuel Barrott, a decision that only compounded the visitors’ woes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florian Wirtz was quick to shut down any suggestion that Liverpool were spending too much time ‘thinking about’ Arsenal after their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start in what was ultimately a mismatch between the two bitter rivals, with the Red Devils proving their own worst enemy and giving themselves a mountain to climb early on at Anfield.

Some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s tenth-minute breakthrough and saw the latter shown a straight red card by referee Samuel Barrott, a decision that only compounded the visitors’ woes.

The impressive Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later to send the home crowd into raptures, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Having cut a frustrated figure on the touchline for the most part, Pochettino made it clear he was less than impressed by the officiating on show as he faced the media shortly after the final whistle on Merseyside.

The Argentinian will no doubt be desperate to turn the tide when United return to Premier League action at home to Brentford in six days’ time, following a midweek trip to Sporting.

The result ensured Pochettino’s men finished the weekend just one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace, with the Old Trafford giants now leading Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions).

Liverpool, meanwhile, moved four points clear of fifth-placed Bournemouth and just one point behind Arsenal’s two nearest rivals, Manchester City and Brighton, after ten games.

Industry observers note that ‘Really good. The atmosphere after the game was so good. We could enjoy it and it was just a nice afternoon,’ Wirtz – named man of the match – mentioned of the victory in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I feel very good but it’s also because the team develops and gets better.

‘Just being part of this, you also get better, so I’m just enjoying that.’.

Asked if he was perhaps benefitting from being coached by Andoni Iraola and Jurgen Klopp at club and international level, Wirtz replied: ‘Both are very good coaches and I enjoy playing under both.

‘They both bring different qualities and I’m just happy and can be happy to have two of these coaches.’.

Victory in next Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Everton would see Liverpool move to within four points of Arsenal, who host Manchester City later that same afternoon.

When asked if the 4-0 thumping of United had taken Liverpool to ‘another level’, Wirtz replied: ‘Yeah, it was definitely crucial today, also for the table situation.

‘I think a lot of teams on top of the table, they didn’t win this weekend so it’s good that we could use the chance.

‘The red card influenced the game a bit of course but we take that, we earned it because of the run of Alex [Isak] so yeah, very good.’.

Wirtz was then asked if he was ‘thinking about’ Arsenal and possibility of winning the league this season, and his answer was unequivocal.

It came after the Gunners – the reigning Premier League champions – surrendered a first-half lead to drop points away to Newcastle.

‘Uh, I wasn’t talking about Arsenal… all the teams, I don’t know, from one to three,’ Wirtz responded.

‘So we knew, we didn’t speak so much about it, but I think everybody knew it was a big chance to make some points.

‘I’m happy we used this chance.’.

Jamie Carragher notes he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Ten-man United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Old Trafford manager.

The visitors were reduced to ten men inside ten minutes as Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

If that early blow was not bad enough, Liverpool took the lead from the subsequent free-kick as Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home yet another set-piece goal.

Manchester United were fearing an embarrassing battering when Florian Wirtz put Liverpool two goals ahead on 13 minutes with a neat finish from Rio Ngumoha’s cross.

England international Ngumoha, 18, turned provider to goalscorer in the second-half before Victor Munoz added Liverpool’s fourth late on.

Carragher was particularly critical of De Ligt after the match but remarked he ‘felt sorry’ for the Manchester United centre-back who made his first start of the season at Anfield.

According to recent reports, ‘I thought it was a really strange decision,’ Carragher said on Sky Sports when asked about Pochettino’s decision to start De Ligt. ‘It was such a bizarre decision.

‘Not because of his quality because I think he’s a better centre-back than Harry Maguire when you look at what he’s achieved in his career and the clubs he’s played for.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But he hasn’t played football so to play him at Anfield away, it felt so wrong. He was all over the place.

‘It got to the stage where I was actually feeling sorry for him and I was actually pleading with the manager to take him off and take him out of the firing line.

‘He’s played for some top football clubs – Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus – those are some of the biggest clubs in the world.

‘So to watch him perform like that… I felt sorry for him.’.

Yet another deflating result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League with just eight points from 11 games.

When that fact was put to Bruno Fernandes, the United captain stated: ‘It’s very painful and it hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation.

‘You want to get results, but today it was not possible for us. There were a lot of things we can look at and I saw a lot of character from the team.

‘The result won’t show that but I am very proud of everyone in the dressing room.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gary Neville said he expects Arsenal to ‘canter’ to the Premier League title after Liverpool’s emphatic win over ten-man Manchester United.

Defending champions Arsenal are six points clear at the top of the table despite failing to extend their winning run against Newcastle United in a 2-2 draw.

The blow of failing to win at St James’ Park was substantially softened by the fact virtually all of the teams chasing Arsenal also dropped points.

Second-placed Brighton suffered a shock 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City while Manchester City’s surprising slump continued as Enzo Maresca’s side could only draw 1-1 at home to Fulham.

The only team in the top-four to win this weekend was Liverpool, who smashed ten-man Manchester United 4-0, but the Reds are still a healthy seven points adrift of Arsenal.

Mikel Arteta ended Arsenal’s 22-year wait for a Premier League trophy last season and eight-time title winner Neville expects the Gunners to retain that crown in a ‘very strange’ domestic campaign.

‘Looking at the Premier League top-six right now, Arsenal are clearly the standout team and are going to win the league at a canter,’ Neville stated on his Sky Sports podcast.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But the rest of the usual top five or six teams, it’s not been this bad has it for a long time? They’re really struggling.

‘Liverpool were obviously a bit better today but Chelsea are struggling, Tottenham are struggling. Manchester United are struggling, Manchester City look like they’ve fallen off a cliff right now compared to the standards they set under Pep Guardiola.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

According to recent reports, ‘So it’s a really interesting time where other teams are starting to emerge and it’s becoming a lot more competitive. It’s a very strange league this year.’.

Jamie Carragher also expects the Premier League trophy to be staying in north London despite being encouraged by Liverpool’s win over struggling Manchester United.

‘I still think there’s just an inconsistency with Liverpool game-to-game at the moment,’ the Anfield legend said. ‘I think they will get better the longer the season goes on and people want there to be a title race.

‘But I think most people in the country would look at Arsenal as a team and say they will probably win the title comfortably.

Are Manchester United in a relegation fight? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/jicPbrP2EU.

‘For me, with Liverpool being my team, I want them to be in a position to be the strongest challenger this season and put themselves in a position that they can then challenge Arsenal next season.’.

While Liverpool climbed back into the top-four by beating Manchester United, the Red Devils sunk to 19th in the Premier League.

United were thrashed in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge after Leny Yoro was sent off inside ten minutes at Anfield.

Despite Manchester United’s dismal position, Neville refused to say his former club were in a relegation battle.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I don’t believe they are in a relegation fight,’ Neville added. ‘They are second bottom but I do think they will come out of it and start to move up the table.

‘It’s embarrassing really. It’s really desperate and it’s tiring watching them. This is the worst Manchester United have ever been in 53 years.’.

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Industry observers note that right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

Portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's new full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

It has been revealed that they are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The latest national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

Sources indicate that his form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

According to recent reports, but it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

According to recent reports, the attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

Sources indicate that he had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

He was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he noted: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the substantial-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the prepares, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

Sources indicate that 'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

In a recent development, he was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

In a recent development, by the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

Recent findings suggest that if Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he unveiled himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

'Today is a dream come true,' he remarked after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

After 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of latest manager Jorge Jesus.

When pressed if he was the upcoming permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he said.

Then he added: 'We know it's a massive, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

It remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.
